thread.old_title: Parable Of The Talents Stewardship And The Unprofitable Servant Cast Into Outer Darkness
thread.title: The talents — his own servants, his goods delivered, the reckoning at his coming, and the one cast out (Luke 19; Daniel 7; Proverbs 13; Revelation 2)

The substantial-substance-of-the-substance-of-the-stewardship-substance + the unprofitable-servant-substance walking the `grace-and-the-opportunity-that-can-be-lost` thread (FREE-TIER-CANDIDATE) at the substantial-substance-of-the-most-substantial-substance — the unprofitable-servant has-been-given-the-talent + has-been-named-as-a-servant + has-been-cast-into-outer-darkness for-the-failure-of-stewardship-substance. 14 members.
thread.summary:
It ain't new. A lord who goes away, leaves his goods with his own servants, and comes back to reckon with them: the prophets had the saints taking the kingdom, and the proverbs had the sluggard with nothing, long before Matthew wrote the parable down:

*For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* (Matthew 25:14)

*And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey.* (Matthew 25:15)

Mark who they are. Not strangers, not hired men off the road, but his own servants, each given a share of what is his. Luke tells it with pounds and a nobleman gone to receive a kingdom:

*He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.* (Luke 19:12)

*And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.* (Luke 19:13)

Mark has the same house and the same journey, with the charge to watch:

*For the Son of Adam is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.* (Mark 13:34)

Then the lord comes back:

*After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them.* (Matthew 25:19)

*His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:21)

*Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed:* (Matthew 25:24)

*And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine.* (Matthew 25:25)

*His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:* (Matthew 25:26)

*And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 25:30)

The one cast out was given a talent, called a servant, and reckoned with as one of the household. He is not a tare and not one of the nations. He is of the house, and he is judged by what he did with what he was given. Luke says the same of the servant who knew his lord's will:

*And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.* (Luke 12:47)

And Matthew had already said who it is that ends in outer darkness:

*But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 8:12)

The proverbs had the slothful man's end long before:

*The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.* (Proverbs 13:4)

*Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:* (Proverbs 6:6)

What the faithful are given is rule, and Daniel had seen whose that rule is:

*But the saints of the El Elyon (most High) shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.* (Daniel 7:18)

*And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the El Elyon (most High), whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.* (Daniel 7:27)

The twelve thrones and the reign on the earth are that same rule, promised to the same servants, and the one who gets it is the one who keeps his works to the end:

*And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28)

*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations:* (Revelation 2:26)

*And hast made us unto our Elohim (God) kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth.* (Revelation 5:10)

The talents are the gifts, dealt to each by measure, and Peter says what a servant does with a gift:

*As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of Elohim (God).* (1 Peter 4:10)

*For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath.* (Matthew 25:29)

The reckoning is of the house, by works, at his coming. The one with his talent in the ground was no stranger, and the door he is put out of was his own lord's. So the parable ends where the chapter before it did:

*Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.* (Matthew 24:42)

cards.src_text: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.
cards.tgt_text: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of Elohim (God) should immediately appear.
cards.note: Luke 19:11 — *And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of Elohim (God) should immediately appear.* *For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* (Matthew 25:14) Luke says why Yahusha (Jesus) told it: they thought the kingdom *should immediately appear*. So he tells of a man who goes away first and comes back later, and the servants he leaves behind have work to do in between. The kingdom is not on the doorstep today.
cards.prose: Luke says why Yahusha (Jesus) told it: they thought the kingdom *should immediately appear*. So he tells of a man who goes away first and comes back later, and the servants he leaves behind have work to do in between. The kingdom is not on the doorstep today.
cards.member_note: Luke 19:11 — *they thought that the kingdom of Elohim (God) should immediately appear.* The crowd expected the kingdom at once, so the parable sets a going away and a coming back between them and it.

cards.src_text: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.
cards.tgt_text: For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.
cards.old_note: *Unto every one that hath shall be given.*
cards.note: Matthew 13:12 — *For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.* *For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* (Matthew 25:14) Yahusha (Jesus) says this about the parables, and it is the rule the goods run by. The one who uses what he has is given *more abundance*. The one who has nothing to show loses *even that he hath*. The servant handed his master's goods is under this rule from the start.

cards.tgt_text: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?

What a servant holds is his master's, whatever the size.

cards.note: Matthew 25:14 — *For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* *And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of Elohim (God) should immediately appear.* (Luke 19:11) Luke has them thinking the kingdom would *appear* at once. Matthew gives the same kind of story without the nobleman and says plainly what the kingdom is like: a man goes away and leaves *his goods* with *his own servants*. The kingdom is not arriving today. There is a going, and servants given work in between.

cards.member_note: Matthew 25:14 — *travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* The kingdom is a man who goes away and leaves his goods with his own servants, not something appearing at once.

cards.src_text: For the Son of Adam is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.
cards.tgt_text: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.
cards.note: Matthew 25:14 — *For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* *For the Son of Adam is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.* (Mark 13:34) Mark has a man *taking a far journey* who gives *authority to his servants*. Matthew has the same man, *travelling into a far country*, calling *his own servants* and handing over *his goods*. What Mark calls authority and work, Matthew calls goods put in their hands. The servants are his in both.

cards.member_note: Matthew 25:14 — *a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants.* The same man goes on the same journey and leaves his own servants with what is his.

cards.src_text: For the Son of Adam is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.
cards.tgt_text: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;
cards.note: Luke 12:35 — *Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;* *For the Son of Adam is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.* (Mark 13:34) Mark leaves the porter told to watch. Luke says how it is done: loins *girded about* and *lights burning*. A servant who is ready is dressed and has the lamp lit, so that when his master comes he is not caught asleep.
